# Planearby

> A free Vue 3 nearby-aircraft dashboard with Korean, English and Japanese interfaces.

Planearby starts when the page becomes visible and the user grants browser location permission. It polls aircraft positions every five seconds until stopped or the page is closed, with no thirty-second session limit. Background browser power policies can delay polling. Returning to the page triggers a refresh.

The radar plots aircraft relative to a manually selected facing direction or an explicitly enabled phone compass. Aircraft noses indicate received ground track. The default horizontal search radius is 25 km, configured in utils/geo.js; altitude is excluded. Supported Airbus, Boeing and Bombardier models are shown. GLEX, helicopters, ground aircraft, stale positions and unsupported types are excluded. Empty results do not prove there are no nearby aircraft.

An analog split-flap board shows one aircraft and rotates to an unseen aircraft every ten seconds. Track uses three cells and distance four cells. Missing route airports retain NON flap cells. Scheduled-time fields are omitted. Phone and tablet layouts place the radar above the board. Light and dark themes include the board and flap cells. Reduced-motion preferences disable the animation.

Data sources: adsb.lol positions under ODbL 1.0, accessed through this app’s fixed-upstream /api/aircraft server function because the source API lacks browser CORS; adsbdb reference routes; the Air Portal directory for operating Korean airlines; and generated OpenFlights airline and aircraft snapshots. The domestic directory takes precedence over missing or historically reused OpenFlights airline codes and supplies Korean names directly. Airline names and IATA/ICAO pairs are matched from generated datasets, not handwritten airline lists. Callsign-derived airline names and routes are inferred and may differ from the actual operation. No paid data API, API key, login or payment information is sent to data providers. No third-party public CORS relay is used.

Approximate coordinates rounded to three decimal places are sent to the app’s server-function host and adsb.lol. Exact browser coordinates are used locally for distance filtering. App code does not store or log coordinates; hosting and provider policies apply to requests. Theme, language and manual facing preferences are stored locally. Cached routes, deduplication and backoff reduce unnecessary calls. A 403 is shown explicitly and retried after five minutes. Free data access does not guarantee unlimited availability; server-function hosting has its own plan limits.

GitHub Pages deployment is available through npm run deploy after VITE_AIRCRAFT_API_URL is configured to point to a separately deployed api/aircraft.js function. GitHub Pages cannot run server functions. Vite development and preview serve the local function automatically; a Vercel Vite deployment can serve the included Node function at /api/aircraft. The app is prerendered to static HTML and has semantic landmarks, keyboard controls, accessible status messages and generated deployment metadata. It is for personal curiosity, not navigation or safety decisions.

- [adsb.lol data](https://www.adsb.lol/docs/open-data/api/)
- [adsbdb](https://github.com/mrjackwills/adsbdb)
- [OpenFlights](https://openflights.org/data.php)
- [Air Portal airline directory](https://www.airportal.go.kr/airline/airCompanyInfo.do)
